section.title: Summary
section.p: This bulletin outlines the strategy for deprecating older API endpoints, specifically those stemming from version 1 (V1). It’s crucial to minimize disruption to existing customers while preparing for a smooth transition to version 3 (V3) endpoints. This strategy includes communication, documentation updates, and technical adjustments to ensure a minimal impact.

ul.li: Goal:Gradually remove V1 endpoints, prioritizing those with limited usage or functionality.
Prioritization:Start with endpoints that have been superseded by V3 equivalents.
Implementation:Implement a deprecation flag in the API documentation (Swagger). Mark deprecated endpoints with deprecated: true.
Examples:/v2/orderlines/validateRule (This endpoint should be removed. Consider adding a migration path to V3 if feasible.)
Target Audience:All users of the APIs, including Canoe (internal customer), and any other customers leveraging the APIs.

Communication Channels:Slack/Email:Send a notification to internal consumers (e.g., SIGMA, Jarvis) detailing the deprecation schedule and any necessary actions.API Documentation:Update Swagger documentation to clearly indicate deprecated endpoints.Release Notes:Include deprecation announcements in upcoming release notes.
Migration Path:For endpoints like /v2/orderlines/validateRule, evaluate the possibility of a migration path to the V3 equivalent.
Testing:Thoroughly test all API changes during the deprecation process.
Monitoring:Monitor API usage to identify endpoints that are nearing deprecation.
Documentation:Maintain up-to-date API documentation, clearly highlighting deprecated endpoints.
Implement the deprecated: true attribute within the Swagger definition for all deprecated endpoints. This will help consumers understand the state of the endpoint.
Estimating:This strategy assumes a phased removal of V1 endpoints, acknowledging that not all V1 features will be immediately replaced.
Customer Impact:Minimize disruption to existing customers. Provide ample notice and support during the transition.
